view: This print turns on two things the price cannot see ahead of the release. The first is the size of the distributor consolidation against a revenue bar that already assumes about RMB750m of extra quarterly revenue. The second, which mattered most last year, is whether a dividend comes with the Q3 release. RLX announced a dividend with its Q3 results in November 2024 ($0.01/ADS) and November 2025 ($0.10/ADS, which sent the stock up 10%). None came with Q2 2026, although Q2 2025 had one. Management's August wording was 'systematic share repurchases and dividend distributions, subject to board approvals'. Against that, part of the cash went to the July acquisition, and no buybacks were reported after September 2025 even though the stock trades below cash. A repeat $0.10 would be about a 7% yield on $1.46 and would likely lift the stock off a flow-driven low. No dividend, or a token $0.01, plus a visibly lower gross margin and lower interest income (Q2 non-GAAP net income fell 18% y/y) would extend the slide. The revenue headline is close to a coin flip: the distributor's revenue was never disclosed, so neither the consensus nor I can rebuild it. I found no channel, regulatory or peer data from inside the quarter that tilts the outcome. Smoore's Q3 vaping revenue rose 1.8% y/y, driven by the US, and says little about RLX's Asian and European business. Malaysia's planned vape ban was still not in force in the mid-2026 sources. The price leans slightly up: the stock sits below cash after index-deletion selling, and the dividend has come with the Q3 release two years running. That lean is far short of a recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The outcome rests on an undisclosed board decision (whether a dividend comes with Q3 and its size) and on revenue from a distributor whose financials were never published, against a consensus I could see only as a snippet. Neither can be found from public traces before the release. The below-cash valuation and the mechanical index-deletion selling are old and public. The dividend has come with Q3 two years running, which gives only a slight up lean, nowhere near 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A dividend of about $0.10/ADS or a new buyback with the release would push this toward a clear up move; no capital return plus a gross margin below about 30% would make it a down move.

self_critique: The up lean rests on a two-year pattern of Q3 dividends and on the stock trading below cash, both public and both possibly already in the price, perhaps even read the other way. A market that has sold steadily into the print may know that capital is going to M&A, and Q2 broke the pattern by carrying no dividend. A large revenue beat from consolidation could be dismissed as acquired, while a margin step-down and lower interest income hit EPS. The gap-down-then-recover pattern at the last print means a 13:00 ET exit lands mid-way, so even the right direction may be small.
